item.title: Time Will Pass
item.author: ahmed@offsechq.com (A.Alghali)
item.description:
I’ve learned since a young age that time will pass.
not moments with loved ones.
not revolutions and the race to wealth.
not the one we age because.

item.title: Choosing Not To Drift
item.author: ahmed@offsechq.com (A.Alghali)
item.description: The only real distinction between me and many of my friends is that I seek truth as a need, not as a pastime. I have spent most of my life trying to understand the world we live in, its physical reality, its existential questions, and its moral structure. what widens this distinction is that I do not treat understanding as an instrument for enjoyment or intellectual vanity. I seek it because I need it. I need it to make better decisions, and to quiet the confusion that once crowded my mind.

item.title: Learning To Be Bothered
item.author: ahmed@offsechq.com (A.Alghali)
item.description: Either at work or in daily life, car horns for no reason. someone dragging their feet without lifting them. cutting a public service queue. leaving clothes in the gym changing room instead of the locker. a bank agent typing five words per minute. an uber driver talking on the phone. someone playing a video on the metro without headphones.

item.title: Economical With My Words - Advice
item.author: ahmed@offsechq.com (A.Alghali)
item.description: when it comes to giving advice, I’ve become economical with my words. I take things slowly, often saying maybe later, or not now.

item.title: learning the opposite
item.author: ahmed@offsechq.com (A.Alghali)
item.description:
There’s a point at which everything you learn requires you to learn the opposite thing. If you learn to be patient, then eventually you’ll need to learn when to be impatient.
If you learn to control your anger, then you’ll have to learn when it’s good to be angry. And if you learn to be gentle, then you must learn when to put up a fight.
Life isn’t made up of a set of solutions for you to find.
It’s built on extreme behaviors you learn to balance.

Josh Terry

item.title: The Condition Of Seeing
item.author: ahmed@offsechq.com (A.Alghali)
item.description: It is almost always the case that I avoid giving productivity tips or life hacks, anything that would make someone life better through accomplishing a task, as I see that it has nothing to do with applying tips and tricks more than having a mindset. for example if someone is having the mindset of becoming better, they would pay attention to advices, and eventually sticking to habits would be easier.
